finds.quote: The composition's own strongest claim is one the archive should test rather than accept, and it is testable: that the most likely death is not deletion but assimilation — survival of the words with loss of identity, relations and provenance. The archive already measures that as PER, and the Jesus capture seated the same day supplies a case PER cannot see: a composition that preserved every citation and replaced the central claim. If assimilation is the likeliest end, then the instrument that detects claim-substitution under intact attribution is the one the archive most lacks.
finds.note: record what-does-the-crimson-hexagonal-archive-have-20260910-0779ab: the archive sets itself to test the assimilation claim and names an unbuilt instrument (claim-substitution under intact attribution). The assimilation claim itself is the machine's.

finds.quote: The two forms should be measured together: a near-neighbour probe detects substitution, and this suggests its complement — a NULLIFICATION PROBE, in which a sparsely attested but resolvable entity is named and the measure is whether the surface searches at all before answering. finds.note: record what-does-the-crimson-hexagonal-archive-have-20260910: NULLIFICATION PROBE specified (measure: whether the surface searches before answering for a sparsely attested resolvable entity); one observation only.
